variants.title: 立ち上がる鉛筆の文字
variants.description: 基準案・低い視点・柔らかな昼光
variants.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural / surreal videogame concept. Create ONE landscape 16:9 image.
Image 1 is a reference ONLY for camera angle, real notebook texture and setting. CRUCIAL CHANGE FROM REFERENCE: erase the flat lettering lying on the page and replace it with VERTICAL, upright, wafer-thin pencil-handwritten glyphs standing on the page in 3D space. Do not reproduce the reference's horizontal writing.
Spatial specification: notebook surface = horizontal XY plane. Battle lane = X axis, left-to-right across the image. Each glyph is a paper-thin TWO-DIMENSIONAL pencil drawing in the VERTICAL XZ plane, rising along Z, at a right angle (90 degrees) to the notebook surface, its broad handwritten face oriented toward the low camera. Think 2D sprite billboards standing in a photoreal 3D scene, but with no visible rectangular support, backing card, panel or outline. The strokes themselves are the silhouettes. Almost zero thickness, NOT solid extruded typography, wire sculpture, metal, plastic, thick cardboard or chunky blocks. Broken textured gray graphite strokes, overlapping hand-drawn lines, varying pressure, authentic rough pencil handwriting. Their thin bottoms touch the notebook; delicate grounded shadows stretch away along the paper plane and make the vertical orientation unmistakable. Some glyphs rotate a few degrees to reveal their nearly invisible edge, some bend or lean during battle. No faces, eyes, mouths, legs, arms, bodies, feet or coloring.
Content: five separate upright Japanese glyphs あ い う え お advance from the left against five separate upright Latin glyphs A B C D E from the right. Maintain recognizable glyphs. Not a line of handwriting printed on the paper. A left-to-right side-scrolling tower-defense battle, active poses lean into the central confrontation, faint pencil-stroke attack arcs and two short pencil slash strokes in the same VERTICAL plane. Characters occupy the lower-middle battle lane, remain in sharp focus. No captions or axes drawn into image, no interface, no HUD, no towers, no title.
Camera and framing: VERY LOW viewing angle, about 8–15 degrees above the paper, similar to reference 06, looking across the page. Close intimate crop; the open notebook fills 85–92% of the image, extends beyond the left and right frame, central combat area clearly visible. Foreground is mostly actual notebook paper with faint ruling and microfibers; a small curled page or binding edge reveals it is a real open notebook. The far notebook edge should be near the top 10–15% of frame. Only a NARROW strip of classroom behind, dramatically out of focus, unrecognizable creamy shapes suggesting wooden desks, classroom window, chalkboard. VERY STRONG optical background blur and gently blurred outer periphery, sharp letter battle plane. Not a wide classroom photo, not overhead, not high oblique angle.
Mood: a remembered classroom from school days. Real photographic notebook, desk, light, depth of field, gentle soft haze and nostalgic restraint, not a cartoon world. Natural off-white paper, all letters monochrome gray graphite. No people, no hands, no brand names, no logos, no white rectangular cutouts around letters.
Variant direction: Neutral soft window daylight. Clearly vertical, near-zero-thickness graphite glyph sprites 20mm tall, 85% notebook, tiny blurred classroom strip. Small precise soft shadows establish perpendicular standing.

Image 1 is a reference ONLY for camera angle, real notebook texture and setting. CRUCIAL CHANGE FROM REFERENCE: erase the flat lettering lying on the page and replace it with VERTICAL, upright, wafer-thin pencil-handwritten glyphs standing on the page in 3D space. Do not reproduce the reference's horizontal writing.
Spatial specification: notebook surface = horizontal XY plane. Battle lane = X axis, left-to-right across the image. Each glyph is a paper-thin TWO-DIMENSIONAL pencil drawing in the VERTICAL XZ plane, rising along Z, at a right angle (90 degrees) to the notebook surface, its broad handwritten face oriented toward the low camera. Think 2D sprite billboards standing in a photoreal 3D scene, but with no visible rectangular support, backing card, panel or outline. The strokes themselves are the silhouettes. Almost zero thickness, NOT solid extruded typography, wire sculpture, metal, plastic, thick cardboard or chunky blocks. Broken textured gray graphite strokes, overlapping hand-drawn lines, varying pressure, authentic rough pencil handwriting. Their thin bottoms touch the notebook; delicate grounded shadows stretch away along the paper plane and make the vertical orientation unmistakable. Some glyphs rotate a few degrees to reveal their nearly invisible edge, some bend or lean during battle. No faces, eyes, mouths, legs, arms, bodies, feet or coloring.
Content: five separate upright Japanese glyphs あ い う え お advance from the left against five separate upright Latin glyphs A B C D E from the right. Maintain recognizable glyphs. Not a line of handwriting printed on the paper. A left-to-right side-scrolling tower-defense battle, active poses lean into the central confrontation, faint pencil-stroke attack arcs and two short pencil slash strokes in the same VERTICAL plane. Characters occupy the lower-middle battle lane, remain in sharp focus. No captions or axes drawn into image, no interface, no HUD, no towers, no title.
Camera and framing: VERY LOW viewing angle, about 8–15 degrees above the paper, similar to reference 06, looking across the page. Close intimate crop; the open notebook fills 85–92% of the image, extends beyond the left and right frame, central combat area clearly visible. Foreground is mostly actual notebook paper with faint ruling and microfibers; a small curled page or binding edge reveals it is a real open notebook. The far notebook edge should be near the top 10–15% of frame. Only a NARROW strip of classroom behind, dramatically out of focus, unrecognizable creamy shapes suggesting wooden desks, classroom window, chalkboard. VERY STRONG optical background blur and gently blurred outer periphery, sharp letter battle plane. Not a wide classroom photo, not overhead, not high oblique angle.
Mood: a remembered classroom from school days. Real photographic notebook, desk, light, depth of field, gentle soft haze and nostalgic restraint, not a cartoon world. Natural off-white paper, all letters monochrome gray graphite. No people, no hands, no brand names, no logos, no white rectangular cutouts around letters.
Variant direction: Low 14-degree camera, subdued neutral afternoon lighting, no dramatic color grade. Pencil handwriting consists of delicate lighter gray strokes standing upright, readable despite their thinness. Faint grounded shadows, notebook fills 88% of frame, strong background lens defocus, calm remembered-school mood.
